even more atherogenic than SFA, by not only elevating LDL cholesterol to similar levels but also decreasing HDL cholesterol. As
a result, the ratio of LDL cholesterol to HDL cholesterol is signiﬁcantly higher with a TFA rich diet (2.58) than with a SFA diet
(2.34) or an oleic acid diet (2.02). This greatly enhances the risk of CHD. In controlled trials, each 1% energy replacement of
TFA with SFA, MUFA, or PUFA, respectively, decreased the total cholesterol/HDL cholesterol ratio by 0.31, 0.54, and 0.67.
